subject: Phased reserve tuning worksheet — options and clarifications for UmbraHealth
messages:
From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 05 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phased reserve tuning worksheet — options and clarifications for UmbraHealth

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Following our call yesterday, attached is a concise worksheet that lays out three phased reservation options tailored to the usage profile you shared. The workbook (Umbra_Reserve_Tiers_v2.xlsx) contains model-mix assumptions, a suggested minimum GPU floor, and a 30/60/90-day ramp schedule for each option. High level:

- Option Alpha (conservative): Min floor 16 GPUs, steady ramp to 48 over 12 weeks, prewarm credits for first 30 days, geo-burst disabled.
- Option Beta (balanced): Min floor 32 GPUs, ramp to 128 over 12 weeks with guided burst lanes; includes 25% prewarm credit and a 2-week warm-start runway.
- Option Gamma (aggressive): Min floor 64 GPUs, ramp to 256 in 8 weeks, includes geo-burst and dedicated warm pool (subject to availability).

Key performance assumptions included in the sheet: KV-cache hit rate 45%, average sequence length 128 tokens, production mix 70% chat/30% batched generation. We've modeled p50/p95/p99 token latency and approximate per-token cost for each option.

Immediate asks:
1) Please confirm which option you want us to model against your week-1 traffic (you can paste a sample or a percentile).
2) Confirm whether geo-bursting is a requirement for go-live or optional.
3) Any procurement timing constraints (PO window, finance deadline) we should be aware of.

Next steps: if Beta looks closest to what you expect, we recommend a short 30-minute follow-up to agree warm-start credits and the exact ramp trigger rules (percentile usage thresholds for moving to next tranche).

Attachments: Umbra_Reserve_Tiers_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA_anchors.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this week.

— Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Phased reserve tuning worksheet — options and clarifications for UmbraHealth

Hi Sergio — thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. A few clarifying questions before we lock in a direction: 

1) For Option Beta you list a 25% prewarm credit — can you clarify how that credit is applied? Is it a token credit for the first 30 days or a GPU-time credit for warm pool allocation?
2) We expect our week-1 95th percentile to be around 75 RPS across the two east-coast regions. Can you confirm which ramp triggers map to RPS thresholds in your worksheet?
3) Does the cost model assume any quantization (INT8/4bit) or is it NATIVE FP16 throughput? If quantized, please show a conservative and optimistic cost line.

Also, our procurement team needs to see a clear minimum-guarantee clause and an escape hatch (30-day stepdown). Do you have standard language in SLA_anchors.pdf or should we expect a redline?

Tom, fyi — procurement asked for the PO lead time and whether Redwood can support a mid-contract increase in GPUs without a full contract amendment.

Best,
Alyssa
Senior PM, Infrastructure — UmbraHealth
alyssa.park@umbrahealth.com

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
To: alyssa.park@umbrahealth.com, treynolds@umbrahealth.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 06 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased reserve tuning worksheet — options and clarifications for UmbraHealth

Alyssa — great questions, thank you. Short answers first, then a recommended row-level change in the sheet (I updated the workbook and reattached).

1) Prewarm credit: for Beta the 25% prewarm is expressed as a GPU-time credit — it covers the cost of maintaining the warm pool (allocated vGPU-hours) for the first 30 days. Practically, this offsets warm-pool billing and prevents cold-start throttle during onboarding. Footnote in worksheet clarifies accounting.

2) Ramp triggers: each tranche has an RPS trigger and a utilization trigger. For Beta the tranches are: 32 -> 64 @ 65% sustained utilization OR 95th percentile RPS >= 90; 64 -> 96 @ 75% utilization OR RPS >= 110; 96 -> 128 @ 80% utilization OR RPS >= 140. I added a small 'mapping' tab showing RPS <-> estimated concurrent tokens and model QPS. Use your measured 95th of ~75 RPS as the baseline — Beta should be comfortable at week-1 with 32 min GPUs including a 2-week warm runway.

3) Quantization: cost rows show two lines — FP16 (default conservative), and INT8 (quantized optimistic). For model families where quantization is supported we projected ~30% token-cost decrease; the sheet flags models where quality-impact risk exists.

Procurement items:
- Minimum guarantee / escape hatch: SLA_anchors.pdf contains our standard 30-day stepdown language and a mid-contract growth clause (up to +25% capacity without an amendment, subject to availability). For larger increases we typically add a 30-day notice and rate adjustment.
- PO lead time: standard lead time is 45 days for reserved capacity activation cadence; we can compress to 21 days for an onboarding fee if needed.

I've also added a short 'sensitivity' tab that shows cost delta vs. KV-cache hit rate and average seq length. That tends to be the biggest lever for you (a +15% KV hit rate materially lowers the min GPU need).

Next: Ben and Lauren — can you review the revised sheet and confirm whether we want to recommend Beta + geo-burst opt-in (keeps Beta base, enables geo burst only if we see cross-region failover need)? If so I'll propose formal language and a HubSpot deal update with committed SKU lines.

Attachments: Umbra_Reserve_Tiers_v2.xlsx (updated)

— Sergio

Hi Alyssa / Tom — quick internal + customer note. We've reviewed Sergio's updates and recommend moving forward with Option Beta as the commercial baseline with an opt-in geo-burst addon. Summary of the proposed commercial configuration we will include in the term sheet: 

- Baseline: Option Beta
  - Minimum-guarantee: 32 GPUs (min floor)
  - Ramp schedule: 32 -> 64 -> 96 -> 128 over 12 weeks (triggered by utilization or RPS as detailed by Sergio)
  - Warm-start: 2-week dedicated warm runway; 25% GPU-time prewarm credit applied to first 30 days
  - Quantization: FP16 baseline; INT8 optional with quality review and separate cost line
- Geo-burst: optional addon, charged only when used, capped monthly (geo-burst capacity subject to availability)
- SLA / stepdown: standard 30-day stepdown clause; mid-contract increase up to +25% without amendment; PO lead time 21–45 days (21 with onboarding fee)

Tom/Alyssa — if that aligns with your procurement and launch window, we'll convert to a HubSpot quote (deal UMB-2028-0421) and produce a term sheet + preliminary SOW. Can we confirm target start date (week of July 8) and whether Umbra wants geo-burst included in the initial quote?

If confirmed, Ben will prepare the committed SKU lines and I'll kick off the HubSpot quote and DocuSign draft.

Thanks — Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
